description: Allowlisted control IDs. match decides which IDs apply to a diff. review is the guidance the sensors see in their prompt. The gate does not read review.

controls.label: Change management
controls.review: Use this to describe the change itself: what behavior moved, and whether a reviewer can see the impact from the diff.

controls.label: Logical and physical access
controls.review: Use this when the diff changes who can authenticate or what they are allowed to do. Look for session handling, role checks, and untested deny paths.

controls.label: Change management
controls.review: Use this when the diff should be traceable as a planned change. Name the files that carry it and whether the scope is obvious.

controls.label: Secure coding
controls.review: Use this when application code changes. Look for missing validation, unsafe defaults, and credential material in source.

controls.label: Configuration change control
controls.review: Use this when the diff changes configuration, infrastructure, or application behavior. Name what used to be controlled and what the diff changes.

controls.label: Impact analysis
controls.review: Use this when the diff can affect security or operations. Say who or what is affected and what a reviewer should verify before shipping.

controls.label: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets
controls.review: Use this when added lines contain credentials, keys, or tokens. Report material that looks like a secret even if a pattern check might have missed it.

controls.label: Authentication and session patterns
controls.review: Use this for authentication and session changes. Look for how a session is created, how a token is checked, and what happens when the caller is unauthenticated.

controls.label: Authorization and common vuln patterns
controls.review: Use this for authorization and common vulnerability patterns in auth, IAM, or payments. Look for checks that fail open, missing role gates, and unsafe handling of user input.

controls.label: Safe dependency specification
controls.review: Use this when a manifest or lockfile adds a dependency. Name the package and say whether a human must confirm it is the intended, existing package.
